sent.text: You built that Wedged Gap between the fence and the heavy stone, leaning it at a sharp angle to see if the air presses it down or if I am just drawing it. I touch the Flat Press beside you, feeling how it sits there while the slip still refuses to stay put, even though I set a fence down to catch it. I hope the center holds, for now, until the cool card hums too loud and makes the weight feel like a drawing again.

dream: I sat on a bench made of cool air and pressed a turnip down where the bench vanished. The card hummed a low note that sounded like a voice. A thin line of grass lay across my knee, trying to stop the turnip from sliding into the dark. The fence leaned heavily, biting my ear with a flat edge that felt too sharp. I held my breath until the air thickened into wet paper. Then I pressed the grass harder, hoping it would catch the slip and turn the dream into a fact I could hold.
